title: Cross-role Tool Access Governance and Self-Service Handbook
content:
Summary:

This handbook sets out how access to Redwood internal tools is granted, reviewed and revoked across roles and teams, including the governance model, operational runbook and self-service flows. Audience: people-ops, engineering managers, security reviewers and tool maintainers. We want tool access to be predictable, auditable and quick, without over-permissioning.

Key Principles:
- Least privilege: people get the minimum role their job needs.
- Role-based assignments, with time-boxed exceptions.
- Automate safe, common grants; keep manual oversight for risky ones.
- Every tool has a named owner and escalation path.
- Provisioning, reviews and deprovisioning are tracked centrally.

1) Scope and Definitions
- Tool: any internal SaaS, self-hosted service or repo that needs explicit credentials or permissions (AWS consoles, Jira admin groups, prod Grafana, CI pipelines).
- Role: a named permission set (e.g., developer-readonly, infra-operator).
- Access Request: a request in the Access Portal for a role or tool-specific permission.
- Exception: temporary access outside standard roles, always with an expiration and approver.

2) Ownership and Responsibilities
- Tool Owner: maintains the role catalog, documents permissions, defines self-service gates, handles escalations.
- People Ops: runs onboarding/offboarding orchestration, review cadence and top-level policy.
- Security: sets exception policy, approves high-risk tools, runs audits.
- Manager: confirms business need for each request.

3) Access Model
- Role Catalog: canonical role list per tool, kept in the Access Portal.
- Self-Service Roles: low-risk, granted instantly (docs-edit, ci-reader).
- Request-and-Approve Roles: medium-risk, need manager approval (staging-deploy, metrics-writer).
- Manual Approval Roles: high-risk, need security review (prod-admin, billing-admin).

4) Standard Provisioning Flow
1. User submits a request in the Access Portal (or CLI).
2. Self-service roles are granted immediately and logged; the user is notified.
3. Manager-approval roles: the manager gets an approval email and must respond within 72 business hours; approved requests provision automatically.
4. Security-approval roles: queued for a security reviewer; expected SLA is 3 business days.
5. Every grant records requester, approver, justification, expiration (for exceptions) and ticket ID.

5) Approval Matrix (sample)
| Tool Category | Example Tools | Typical Role Name | Approval Path | Max SLA for Approval | Expiration Policy |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Low risk | Docs, Internal Wiki | docs-edit | Self-service | Instant | Persistent (attached to employment) |
| Medium risk | Staging CI, Dev DB | staging-deploy | Manager | 72 business hours | 90 days (auto-renew) |
| High risk | Production infra, Billing | prod-admin | Manager + Security | 3 business days | 14 days (explicit extension only) |

6) Exception and Emergency Access
- Incident mitigation uses the Fast-Track Exception flow:
  1) Requester files an incident-tagged access request with justification and incident ID.
  2) The on-call approver (manager or incident commander) can issue an 8-hour temporary token through the Access Portal.
  3) Security is notified within 1 hour and either converts the grant to a formal exception or revokes it.
- Emergency grants are logged and reviewed in the incident postmortem.

7) Deprovisioning and Offboarding
- Timeline:
  - Day 0: interactive access disabled within 24 hours of the HR offboarding signal.
  - Day 1: short-lived API tokens invalidated; persistent service accounts rotated where needed.
  - Day 7: cloud console roles removed; outstanding owner responsibilities backed up.
- Managers reassign ownership before final removal.
- People-ops runs weekly deprovisioning reports; security verifies monthly.

8) Periodic Access Reviews
- High-risk roles: quarterly.
- Medium-risk: twice a year.
- Low-risk: annually.
- Process: Access Portal report -> owner validates or starts deprovisioning -> people-ops enforces within 7 business days.

9) Tool Onboarding Checklist (Tool Owners)
1. Define roles as least-privilege sets.
2. Document them in the Role Catalog on the owner page.
3. Mark roles as self-service or approval-required.
4. Publish an onboarding runbook with contacts and SLOs.
5. Register the owner and escalation email in the Access Portal.
6. Provide a test account and verification steps.

10) Technical Integration Patterns
- Preferred: SSO plus SCIM group sync.
- Without SCIM: an API-based provisioning endpoint with scoped tokens and change tracking.
- Example access request payload (JSON):
{
  "requester": "user@redwood.com",
  "tool": "grafana-prod",
  "role": "viewer",
  "justification": "Oncall rotation",
  "expires_at": "2025-02-28T23:59:00Z"
}
- Example CLI:
$ rwd-access request --tool grafana-prod --role viewer --justification "oncall"

11) Monitoring, Auditing and KPIs
- KPIs: median time-to-provision, percent self-service, active exceptions, time-to-deprovision after offboarding.
- Cadence: weekly provisioning dashboard; monthly CSV audit exports to the security vault.
- Audit check: no more than 5% of production-admin grants older than 30 days without re-approval.

12) Dispute Resolution
- Disputed grants or removals go to people-ops with the ticket ID; people-ops brings together the manager, tool owner and security to decide within 5 business days.

13) Sample Runbook: Prod-Read Access (Manager-Approved)
1. Manager submits the request with justification.
2. Portal notifies the tool owner and requests manager approval.
3. Provisioning job runs (SCIM or API) on approval.
4. Access granted, audit log written, requester and manager notified.
5. After 90 days a renewal task is created for the manager.

14) Implementation Roadmap
- Q2 2025: SCIM integrations for the top 5 tools.
- Q3 2025: Delegated team-admin roles for large product groups.
- Q4 2025: Exception analytics dashboard.

15) Appendix: Common Role Examples
- developer-readonly: view-only GitHub repos and dev dashboards.
- ci-builder: trigger CI pipelines and write artifacts to staging buckets.
- infra-operator: staging deploys and infra-as-code PRs.
- prod-admin: full production console access (high-risk).

Contact and Escalation
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com
- Security on-call: security-oncall@redwood.com
- Tool owners: listed on each tool owner page in the Access Portal

Change Log
- 2024-11-04: Created by Aisha Patel (initial policy and flows).
- 2025-02-20: Added emergency fast-track flow and approval SLAs (reviewers: Marcus Liu, Sofia Ramirez).
